@@ urbanmen
This is a generalized label for the town and city folk of th northern and southern empires. Urbanmen contain varying d grees of Hillman, Nomad, Woodman, and High Man blood. Th catagory represents men born and raised in major towns an cities.

@@ hysical_haracter
Build: All types, but normally medium. Males average 15 pounds; women, 125 pounds. Coloring: Variations of fair to tan or olive skin. All colors of ha and eyes. Endurance: Average. Height: Males average 5'10"; women, 5'4". Lifespan: Moderate, averaging 65-85 years. Resistance: Normal. Special Abilities: None.

@@ ulture
Clothing & Decoration: Various types of elaborate or practic wool and linen garb, including cloaks, boots, etc. Tunics a worn in warmer areas; shirts and pants or leggings are worn in cooler locales. Some imported silks and fine cottons are in evidence. Fears & Inabilities: Nothing special, aside from local superstitions. Lifestyle: Urban folk are a varied, rather cosmopolitan lot. Many are from mercantile or guild backgrounds and some have dealt with enchantments. Marriage Pattern: Monogamous. The line is traced through either the male or female. Religion: Variations of subdued rituals with some orga- nized cults and shrines. Most have reverence for local or community spirits, although the principal worship fo- cuses on the “True Gods.”

@@ ther_actors
Demeanor: Practical, aggressive, hard-working, and in- quisitive. Language: Starting Languages: Common-speech (S8/ W6). Allowed Adolescence Development: Common- speech (S10/W10), High-speech (S8/W8), Sea-speech (S8/W8), Grey-elvish (S8/W8). Prejudices: Urbanmen are worldly enough to deal with most outsiders. They hate no race, aside from the Orcs. Professions: No special notes. Special Skills: Everyman: all skills in the Urban category; Restricted: none.
